$comment: The editorial content the product is made of, as seed rows for content_items.
Committed for the same reason pricing.rows.json is: CI builds an empty
database every run, so the rows have to live in the repository. Generated
once from the seven src/data TypeScript modules this replaces, which is why
every code below is the id those modules already used - an admin edit keyed
to p1 survives a re-seed because the seeder matches on (kind, code).
The seeder writes text and order. It never writes status on a row that
already exists, and it never deletes: pulling something is a decision a
person made about what the public sees, and a seed run must not reverse it.
KNOWN DUPLICATION: every one of the ten example rows is byte-identical to
one of the ten community posts in src/data/community.ts - same seed, same
prompt. They were always two views of one placeholder set. Explore reads
examples today so they are seeded, but when community posts become real
rows in posts, this kind should be deleted rather than maintained.
